Team —

As we prep for the QBR next week I want a short, aligned decision set on hiring rules of engagement for the next 60 days. Finance has flagged a tighter headcount envelope; leadership wants clarity on: (1) which reqs we approve to post now, (2) which backfills are mandatory for ops continuity, and (3) any freeze exceptions (customer-impact or legal/regulatory).

I attached a worksheet with the current queue and my initial prioritization. Quick asks: please reply with your accept/reject for the three high-priority reqs (REQ-3245 infra lead, REQ-3291 SRE backfill, REQ-3312 product growth PM) and any conditions (e.g., must be IC vs manager, contractor interim ok).

Agenda for sign-off call (30m) tomorrow at 3pm PT if we need it:
- Confirm mandatory backfills
- Approve up to 3 open headcount requests to post
- Define freeze exceptions process and owner

If I don't hear objections by EOD I'll move the infra and SRE backfills to approved status and ask Recruiting to start.

Thanks —
Marissa
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Marissa —

+1 to your framing. A couple of clarifications from my side:
- REQ-3245 (infra lead): approve to post now. Critical for model serving SLAs and customer commitments (we've got two pilot customers queued for Dedicated in May).
- REQ-3291 (SRE backfill): approve as mandatory backfill. Oncall and incident triage coverage is non-negotiable.
- REQ-3312 (product growth PM): I recommend we hold to hiring freeze unless we can free up contractor budget; growth is important but lower immediate risk.

One operational ask: if we approve REQ-3245 we should allow recruiting to run a contractor for up to 12 weeks to shorten time-to-hire. That saves us ramp and reduces SLA exposure.

-Markus
